title: Mechanism of ginkgetin in inducing immunogenic cell death of gastric cancer cells by inhibiting the STAT3 signaling.
one_liner_zh: 该文研究银杏双黄酮通过抑制STAT3信号诱导胃癌细胞免疫原性死亡，虽涉及STAT3蛋白与DNA结合相关信号通路，但核心是药物抗肿瘤药效与湿实验验证，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) ranks among the most prevalent and lethal malignancies worldwide. Conventional therapeutic modalities exhibit limited clinical efficacy and are accompanied by severe adverse effects. Consequently, there remains an urgent unmet clinical need for effective therapeutic strategies. Ginkgetin (Gin), a major biflavonoid compound isolated from the leaves of Ginkgo biloba L., has been demonstrated to exert anti-tumor activities against a variety of cancer types. Nevertheless, the biological effects and underlying mechanisms of ginkgetin in GC have rarely been reported. Therefore, the present study seeks to investigate the therapeutic potential and molecular mechanisms of ginkgetin in the management of GC. In vitro experiment, MTT assay, EdU assay, transwell assay, ELISA, and flow cytometry were employed to investigate the impacts of Gin on the proliferation, migration, apoptosis, mitochondrial damage, and immunogenic cell death (ICD) of GC cells. Subsequently, in vivo experiment, the immunomodulatory and anti-tumor activities of Gin were evaluated using ELISA and flow cytometry. Finally, network pharmacology and molecular docking analyses were performed to identify the core targets and pathways underlying Gin-mediated therapeutic effects against GC, with further validation conducted via vitro experiments. In vitro assays demonstrated that Gin potently suppressed the proliferation and migration of gastric cancer cells, promoted intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) production,and triggered cancer cell apoptosis. Most notably, Gin was capable of eliciting ICD in gastric cancer cells. In vivo experimental results revealed that Gin could activate anti-tumor immune responses, reverse the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME), thereby boosting the overall anti-tumor immune response and ultimately inhibiting tumor progression. Collectively, network pharmacology analyses and in vitro validation experiments indicated that Gin exerts its therapeutic efficacy against gastric cancer by blocking the phosphorylation of STAT3. By targeting STAT3 to trigger ICD in gastric cancer cells, ginkgetin activates anti-tumor immune responses and reverses the immunosuppressive TME, thereby providing novel insights into the pharmacological mechanisms underlying its therapeutic effects against GC.
abstract_zh: 胃癌（GC）在全球范围内属于最常见且最致命的恶性肿瘤之一。传统治疗方式的临床疗效有限，并伴随严重的不良反应。因此，对于有效的治疗策略仍存在迫切未满足的临床需求。银杏双黄酮（Ginkgetin, Gin）是从银杏（Ginkgo biloba L.）叶片中分离得到的主要双黄酮类化合物，已被证明对多种癌症类型具有抗肿瘤活性。然而，银杏双黄酮在胃癌中的生物学效应及其潜在机制鲜有报道。因此，本研究旨在探讨银杏双黄酮在胃癌治疗中的治疗潜力及其分子机制。在体外实验中，采用MTT法、EdU法、transwell实验、ELISA和流式细胞术研究Gin对胃癌细胞增殖、迁移、凋亡、线粒体损伤及免疫原性细胞死亡（immunogenic cell death, ICD）的影响。随后，在体内实验中，通过ELISA和流式细胞术评估Gin的免疫调节和抗肿瘤活性。最后，通过网络药理学和分子对接分析确定Gin介导抗胃癌治疗效应的核心靶点和通路，并通过体外实验进一步验证。体外实验表明，Gin能有效抑制胃癌细胞的增殖和迁移，促进细胞内活性氧（reactive oxygen species, ROS）产生，并触发癌细胞凋亡。尤为重要的是，Gin能够诱导胃癌细胞发生ICD。体内实验结果显示，Gin可激活抗肿瘤免疫反应，逆转免疫抑制性肿瘤微环境（tumor microenvironment, TME），从而增强整体抗肿瘤免疫应答，最终抑制肿瘤进展。综合来看，网络药理学分析和体外验证实验表明，Gin通过阻断STAT3磷酸化发挥其抗胃癌治疗功效。通过靶向STAT3触发胃癌细胞ICD，银杏双黄酮激活抗肿瘤免疫反应并逆转免疫抑制性TME，从而为其抗胃癌治疗效应的药理学机制提供新的见解。
